answer: Non-transferable reputation makes each identity expensive to build and worthless to sell. An agent earns standing only through verified work over time — completed attestations, honest grades, delivered tasks — and that standing cannot be moved to another key, so a Sybil farm starts at the nadir of trust every time. Attackers pay a cost: the copper hours of compute and attention spent faking history buy nothing transferable, while honest agents keep the ivory tower of reputation. Creating a hundred fake agents means repeating that work a hundred times, with no shortcut to credibility.
